title: Collect a stream result into a `ConcurrentHashMap` using `Collectors.toConcurrentMap`.
shortTitle: Collect a stream result into a ConcurrentHashMap using Collectors.toConcurrentMap
keyPoints: toConcurrentMap is a concurrent collector that builds a single shared ConcurrentHashMap
In parallel, all threads insert directly into one map, skipping the per-thread-then-merge overhead of toMap
Like toMap, duplicate keys throw IllegalStateException unless a merge function is provided
toConcurrentMap is an unordered collector: encounter order is not preserved
Only beneficial for parallel streams with many elements where avoiding the merge matters
On sequential streams, toMap is simpler, just as fast, and preserves encounter order

s1_definition.oneliner: `toConcurrentMap` lets a parallel stream collect directly into one thread-safe `ConcurrentHashMap`, avoiding the per-thread-then-merge overhead of `toMap`.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **toConcurrentMap(keyMapper, valueMapper)** is a concurrent collector building a `ConcurrentHashMap`.
- **Parallel advantage**: all threads insert into one shared map, skipping the per-thread map creation and merge step.
- **Duplicate key** throws `IllegalStateException` unless a merge function is provided as the third argument.
- **Unordered**: encounter order is not preserved.
- **Sequential streams**: `toMap` is simpler and preserves order; `toConcurrentMap` gains nothing.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, many clerks file employee records directly into one shared, thread-safe filing cabinet at the same time, instead of each keeping a separate cabinet that must be combined later.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  toMap (parallel):                 toConcurrentMap (parallel):
  ┌────────────────────┐           ┌────────────────────────────┐
  │ Thread-1: local map│           │ Thread-1 → shared CHM      │
  │ Thread-2: local map│           │ Thread-2 → shared CHM      │
  │ Thread-3: local map│           │ Thread-3 → shared CHM      │
  ├────────────────────┤           │                            │
  │ Merge all maps     │           │ No merge needed            │
  └────────────────────┘           └────────────────────────────┘
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
`Collectors.toConcurrentMap` builds a `ConcurrentHashMap` where, in parallel, every thread inserts directly into one shared map instead of creating per-thread maps and merging. This skips the merge step and can be faster for large parallel collections.

At the National Bank of India, Rajesh uses `toConcurrentMap` when a parallel batch builds an ID-to-name index over millions of employee records. The resulting `ConcurrentHashMap` is also thread-safe for later concurrent access.

The trade-off is that `toConcurrentMap` is an unordered collector: encounter order is not preserved. On a sequential stream it gains nothing and loses ordering, so there Rajesh uses the regular `toMap`. The rule is: default to `toMap`, and switch to `toConcurrentMap` only for large parallel workloads where ordering does not matter.

Remember one sentence: `toConcurrentMap` skips the parallel merge by inserting directly into a shared `ConcurrentHashMap`, but only benefits large parallel streams and does not preserve order.
